claims.statement: Deep Agents follows a trust-the-LLM model, so containment belongs in installed tool implementations, backends, or sandboxes; HITL is opt-in, StateBackend does not execute shell commands, and LocalShellBackend is an explicit higher-power opt-in.

FilesystemPermission validates absolute patterns, resolves ordinary read/write decisions by ordered first match with allow as the default, and for a FilesystemBackend checks both requested and symlink-resolved paths before execution or result filtering; confirmed leaf deletion keeps first-match behavior, whereas potentially recursive deletion conservatively blocks any overlapping deny-write pattern.

Deep Agents converts filesystem interrupt permissions into HumanInTheLoopMiddleware routing, with user interrupt_on entries overriding generated entries by tool name: exact-tool predicates consider requested and symlink-resolved candidates and suppress review on denial, while bulk predicates conservatively route intersecting anchored scopes, missing or current-directory paths, absolute glob patterns, and relative glob patterns containing parent traversal; approved or edited calls still re-enter tool-level denial enforcement.

Talon's ToolApprovalStore persists a validated exact-name boolean policy in a bounded regular non-symlink JSON file; enabled entries yield approve/reject interrupt configuration, updates are locked revision compare-and-swap operations, and each invocation binds an immutable snapshot and its matching graph so in-flight work is isolated from saved changes.

Talon derives the operator context required to change approval policy from trusted channel exposure rather than request metadata, requires active invocation context as well, keeps approval and external authorization callbacks separate, and accepts channel approval replies only from the initiating sender while reactions also require matching provider, conversation, prompt message, and sender.

Scheduled invocations and background-result deliveries do not retain an interactive approval or OAuth path: the host marks delivery as unattended and withholds both handlers, while the runtime independently clears operator context for cron or delivery and auto-rejects protected calls in those contexts, including when an approval handler is injected.

Detached background subagents clear operator and authorization context and report an interrupted protected action as not run; cron-only inline delegation instead executes within its already unattended caller, disallows nested delegation, and cannot inherit an interactive approval or authorization handler.
TalonHost stores one pending approval future by agent conversation, prompts through the channel, removes the pending entry when it resolves, and only completes it from an accepted reply or reaction.

Talon creates its default approval policy only when the policy file is missing, and that default enables send_message alongside policy, conversation, MCP-server, and async-task management tools; an existing valid policy is retained unchanged.

Talon is an experimental alpha runtime rather than a production or enterprise security boundary; it lacks complete production-grade HITL approval policy, channel administrator controls, and multi-tenant isolation, and its opt-in sandbox does not cover MCP tools.

Declarative subagents, including forked declarative subagents, inherit parent filesystem permissions and top-level interrupt_on only when their specifications omit those fields; supplied permissions replace the parent rules, supplied interrupt_on replaces the inherited map, while compiled and remote subagents inherit neither the parent filesystem permissions nor interrupt configuration.

Harness-profile excluded_tools removes names from model-facing tool lists and rejects matching calls at the tool boundary, but is explicitly not a security surface; FilesystemMiddleware and SubAgentMiddleware are protected scaffolding that excluded_middleware cannot remove.

A nonempty filesystem permission set is rejected for an execution-capable backend because `execute` has no tool-level permission enforcement; the exception is a CompositeBackend only when every rule path is scoped to a configured route prefix.

DeepAgentRuntime scopes the active graph, approval snapshot, operator status, authorization handler, message handler and progress budget, scheduled-turn flag, cron origin, and pending background results to one invocation, and resets all of them so completion, failure, or cancellation cannot leak request context into a later invocation.

Each Talon scheduled job run is serialized under its job conversation lock, uses a fresh cron thread ID, and is bounded to 1,800 seconds; a timeout repairs the interrupted thread and fails the run, so a later fire starts a new thread. Scheduled delegations run inline with nested delegation disabled, bounded concurrency, and a per-delegation timeout rather than becoming detached background work.

dcode resolves per-thread Manual, Auto, and YOLO modes from a validated Store record keyed by the SHA-256 of the thread ID; typed autonomous modes require a valid thread-bound key and record, while malformed or unavailable control state fails closed to Manual.

dcode Auto reuses the gated HITL map but replaces stock HITL with deterministic policy and classifier review: a classifier response must cover every reviewed action exactly once before binding to tool-call IDs, classifier-unavailable calls are denied without execution, and invalid decision/control state falls back to Manual human approval.

dcode requires an explicit, versioned acknowledgement before its switcher enters YOLO and treats absent, corrupt, or unreadable acknowledgement state as unacknowledged; acknowledgement and Auto first-enable notice state share a private, locked, atomically written local file.

AsyncSubAgent launches independent remote Agent Protocol runs and records their task/thread state locally; a remote interruption is surfaced as waiting, but the user must answer the child directly and the parent cannot approve it.

dcode's first-enable Auto modal is a pre-activation disclosure: it identifies the classifier reviewer and, when distinct, says it is not the code-writing model; Enter records the notice and then requires a successful live-mode write, while cancellation or modal/write failure leaves Auto inactive.

The auto-added general-purpose subagent is assembled independently but receives the parent permissions and merged filesystem-derived and caller interrupt configuration; it is skipped when disabled by profile or replaced by a same-name inline subagent, and it inherits only caller middleware that replaces a default general-purpose slot.

When Talon runs at verbosity 2 or 3, it exposes the explicit `send_message` progress tool; the default exact-name approval policy routes that tool through the ordinary approval flow before its request-scoped channel handler delivers it. This routing does not expose the tool at lower verbosity, authorize arbitrary recipients, or provide containment.
